Simulated manifolds

Source: R/simulate.R
sim_manifolds.Rd

The Swiss roll and S-curve manifolds of Gashler, Ventura and Martinez (2008), with their intrinsic (two-dimensional) coordinates, to test dimensionality reduction methods.

Usage

sim_swiss_roll(n = 2000, noise = 0)

sim_s_curve(n = 2000, noise = 0)

Arguments

n

The number of points.

noise

The standard deviation of Gaussian noise added to the coordinates x, y and z.

Value

A tibble with n rows and the columns x, y, z (the coordinates in three dimensions) and u, v (the intrinsic coordinates). The points are ordered by u.

Details

For the Swiss roll, \(t_i = 8i/n + 2\) for \(0 \le i < n\), and $$x_i = t_i \sin(t_i), \quad y_i \sim U(-6, 6), \quad z_i = t_i \cos(t_i).$$ Its intrinsic coordinates are the arc length along the roll, \(u_i = (\sinh^{-1}(t_i) + t_i \sqrt{t_i^2 + 1}) / 2\), and \(v_i = y_i\).

For the S-curve, \(t_i = (2.2i - 0.1)\pi / n\), and $$x_i = t_i, \quad y_i = \sin(t_i), \quad z_i \sim U(0, 2).$$ Its intrinsic coordinates are the arc length along the curve, \(u_i = \int_0^{t_i} \sqrt{\cos^2(w) + 1} \, dw\), and \(v_i = z_i\). (The paper gives \(v_i = y_i\), a misprint since \(y_i\) is a function of \(u_i\).)

References

Gashler, M., Ventura, D. and Martinez, T. (2008). Iterative non-linear dimensionality reduction with manifold sculpting. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 20, 513–520.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim_swiss_roll(5)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>       x      y      z     u      v
#>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1  1.82 -2.81  -0.832  2.96 -2.81 
#> 2 -1.59 -1.53  -3.23   7.72 -1.53 
#> 3 -4.59  0.874  2.44  14.9   0.874
#> 4  3.36  4.90   5.91  24.7   4.90 
#> 5  7.18 -3.58  -4.36  36.9  -3.58 
sim_s_curve(5)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>         x       y     z       u     v
#>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 -0.0628 -0.0628 1.80  -0.0888 1.80 
#> 2  1.32    0.969  1.89   1.66   1.89 
#> 3  2.70    0.426  1.32   3.21   1.32 
#> 4  4.08   -0.809  1.26   5.07   1.26 
#> 5  5.47   -0.729  0.124  6.54   0.124
